description: Dashboard Productivity zone (issue #169): pure web-layer composition that fills the empty `productivity` slot with a weekly completion snapshot (C), in-progress Epic progress bars (useEpics), a by-week completion trend (C endpoint via a new web consumer, inline SVG — no chart lib), and a collapsed investment panel (D, degrading to an empty state). No new server endpoint or domain query.

tasks.title: Weekly completion snapshot section
tasks.spec: specs/dashboard-productivity/spec.md#Productivity zone renders the weekly completion snapshot
tasks.description: Add a `SnapshotRow` component under `packages/web/src/pages/dashboard/productivity/` that reads the existing `useCompletionSnapshot()` (from `entities/issue/lib/completion-snapshot.ts`) and renders this week's `completed` / `failed` / `new` counts, each labeled. Reuse the existing hook unchanged — do not add a new data path. Include the zero-counts-stay-visible behavior and a per-section empty state when there are no issues.
acceptanceCriteria: `SnapshotRow` renders the three counts returned by `useCompletionSnapshot()` labeled as completed, failed, and new.
When the snapshot returns all zeros for the week, the zeros are rendered visibly (the row is not hidden or removed).
When the project has no issues, the section renders a meaningful empty state rather than a blank block.
Counts come only from `useCompletionSnapshot()`; no new fetch, endpoint, or domain query is introduced by this section.
Co-located component tests cover the labeled-counts case, the all-zero case, and the no-issues empty state.
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` pass.
tasks.notes: Per design D3: keep the client-derivation snapshot (`updatedAt` approximation) — swapping it to the endpoint is an explicit Non-Goal deferred to #165's reservation. This section is self-contained and parallel to T-002/T-003/T-004.

tasks.title: In-progress Epic progress bars section
tasks.spec: specs/dashboard-productivity/spec.md#Productivity zone renders in-progress Epic progress bars
tasks.description: Add an `EpicProgressList` component under `packages/web/src/pages/dashboard/productivity/` that reads the existing `useEpics()`, filters to `EpicStatus.Active` (in-progress), sorts by priority then by `deliveredCount/totalIssueCount`, and renders up to a small cap (start with 3) progress bars reusing the exact width-% bar pattern from `packages/web/src/pages/epics/ui/EpicListPage.tsx` (lines ~112-121). Guard `totalIssueCount === 0` to render 0% fill without dividing by zero. Render the Epic-progress empty state when fewer than 2 in-progress Epics exist.
acceptanceCriteria: When `useEpics()` returns ≥2 Epics with `status === 'active'`, the section renders progress bars for at least two of them, each filled proportionally to `deliveredCount / totalIssueCount`.
When fewer than 2 in-progress Epics exist, the section renders an Epic-progress empty state (not a single partial bar presented as the full view).
An in-progress Epic with `totalIssueCount === 0` renders an empty (0%) bar with no divide-by-zero / NaN.
Data comes only from `useEpics()`; no new fetch, endpoint, or domain query is introduced.
Co-located component tests cover: ≥2 bars with proportional fill, the <2 empty state, and the zero-total guard.
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` pass.
tasks.notes: Per design D6. Open design OQ3/OQ4: 'in-progress' defaults to `EpicStatus.Active` only; cap defaults to 3 with a '+N more' affordance if more active Epics exist. The bar visual MUST mirror EpicListPage to stay consistent with the rest of the app.

tasks.title: Completion trend section (endpoint consumer + inline SVG sparkline)
tasks.description: Add a web consumer for the ALREADY-SHIPPED endpoint: `fetchCompletionTrend(projectId)` + a `useCompletionTrend()` TanStack Query hook under `packages/web/src/entities/issue/api/`, calling `GET /api/projects/{projectRef}/issues/metrics/completion?bucket=week` (hard-code `bucket=week`; query key `['issues','metrics','completion','week', projectId]`; modest `staleTime` ~60s). Then add a `CompletionTrend` component under `packages/web/src/pages/dashboard/productivity/` that plots the `completed` count over the returned 12 weekly buckets as an inline `<svg>` sparkline (a `<polyline>` plus a zero baseline; minimal, no axes chrome beyond the satisfaction signal). No third-party charting library. Empty state when there are no buckets / no data. No configurable time range.
acceptanceCriteria: `useCompletionTrend()` calls the existing `GET .../issues/metrics/completion?bucket=week` endpoint; no new server route, controller, or query is added (verify by grep — no new server-side file).
The trend visualization renders one point per returned weekly bucket reflecting the `completed` count, in bucket order, as an inline SVG polyline.
The fixed by-week bucketing is used as-is; the UI exposes no custom bucket-size or custom time-range control.
No charting dependency is added to the web package (verify `packages/web/package.json` gains no charting lib).
When the endpoint returns no buckets / all-zero data, the section renders a meaningful empty state rather than a broken chart.
Co-located tests cover the hook (mocked fetch returning dense 12-week buckets) and the sparkline rendering + empty state.
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` pass.
tasks.notes: Per design D4 + D5. This is a new web CONSUMER of an existing endpoint (shipped by #165), explicitly permitted by the 'no new domain query' Non-Goal, which scopes to server-side queries/endpoints. The endpoint returns dense buckets: `{ bucket, window:{from,to}, buckets:[{boundary, completed, failed}, ...] }`. Plot `completed` only for v1 (design OQ5).

tasks.title: Investment panel (collapsed by default, caliber annotation, D-degradation)
tasks.spec: specs/dashboard-productivity/spec.md#Investment section is collapsed by default with caliber annotation
tasks.description: Add an `InvestmentPanel` component under `packages/web/src/pages/dashboard/productivity/` that is collapsed by default on first render and, when expanded, shows a caliber-annotation slot that identifies the window/population of the displayed figures (e.g. token/cost aggregation basis). Because D's (#166) aggregated usage surface is absent from the codebase (verified: no aggregation endpoint or hook exists, only per-session `AgentSessionUsage`), render an explicit labeled 'data unavailable' empty state at launch. Build the panel structurally complete (collapse/expand + caliber slot) so it is wire-ready: when D's hook lands, only the body swaps from empty state to figures.
acceptanceCriteria: The panel is collapsed on first render; its detailed figures are not visible without an explicit user expand action.
Expanding the panel reveals a caliber annotation that identifies what window or population the figures cover (the annotation slot is present and labeled, not omitted).
At launch the panel renders an explicitly labeled 'data unavailable' empty state (not a blank panel) because D's aggregated usage surface is not present.
No new server endpoint or domain query is introduced; no client-side usage rollup that loads all project sessions (which would be a new query path).
Co-located component tests cover: default-collapsed state, expand reveals caliber annotation, and the D-unavailable empty state.
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` pass.
tasks.notes: Per design D7 + risk R1. The panel is wire-ready for D: when a usage aggregation hook becomes available, swap the empty-state body for figures — the collapse/expand + caliber layout stays. Do NOT compute a client-side rollup from per-session AgentSessionUsage (that would require loading all sessions = a new query, violating the Non-Goal). Flag the D-surface absence as design Open Question 1.

tasks.title: Productivity zone composition + Dashboard slot mount
tasks.spec: specs/dashboard-shell/spec.md#Dashboard provides four zone mount-point slots
tasks.description: Add `ProductivityZone.tsx` (index) under `packages/web/src/pages/dashboard/productivity/` that composes the four section components from T-001..T-004 (each already owning its per-section empty state). In `packages/web/src/pages/dashboard/ui/DashboardPage.tsx`, swap the `productivity` slot from `DashboardZonePlaceholder` to `<ProductivityZone/>`, KEEPING the slot wrapper's stable `data-testid="dashboard-zone-productivity"` and `data-zone="productivity"` attributes (design D2). Update `packages/web/src/pages/dashboard/ui/DashboardPage.test.tsx` so the productivity slot asserts the zone content is now present while the Attention/Pulse/Digest slots remain empty placeholders, and add an all-data-empty case asserting four labeled empty states (no blank panel).
acceptanceCriteria: The Dashboard `productivity` slot renders `<ProductivityZone/>`; it no longer renders the generic `DashboardZonePlaceholder`.
The slot wrapper retains `data-testid="dashboard-zone-productivity"` and `data-zone="productivity"` (slot identity stays stable for the dashboard-shell contract).
The Attention, Pulse, and Digest slots still render as empty placeholders (unchanged).

The zone composes only the four existing data sources (`useCompletionSnapshot`, `useCompletionTrend`, `useEpics`, and the investment panel); grep confirms no new fetch/endpoint/domain query is introduced by the zone beyond the four section hooks.
When all data sources are empty, the zone renders four labeled per-section empty states (no blank/broken panel).
`DashboardPage.test.tsx` is updated and passes: productivity slot has zone content, the other three slots are still empty placeholders, and the all-empty case renders four empty states.
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` pass.
tasks.notes: Per design D1, D2, D8 and the MODIFIED dashboard-shell requirement. This task is the single point that flips the productivity slot from empty placeholder to filled and therefore satisfies the dashboard-shell delta. Coordinate file creation under pages/dashboard/productivity/ with T-001..T-004 (each owns its own component file; this task owns the index + the DashboardPage swap + the existing dashboard test update).
